# /visual-development

## Purpose

Produce the reference images every page conditions on: the look page that
fixes the drawing style, the character sheets that fix identity, the
location plates, and the prop references. Each candidate is generated from
the bibles, opened, checked against them, and offered to the user. An
approved image becomes a master, is registered in the reference manifest
with one default role, and from then on outranks any prompt.

## Use When

- The bibles are in `review` or `approved` and list planned sheets that do
  not exist yet.
- A bible changed and a master no longer matches it. The new sheet is a new
  version; the old one is marked `superseded`.
- A review traced an identity failure to a missing reference, such as a
  secondary character who never got a sheet.

## Inputs

- `target` (ID, optional): a single `CHAR_*`, `LOC_*`, `PROP_*`, or `LOOK_*`;
  default is every entity with planned sheets that are not registered.
- `provider` (string, optional, default `default_providers.image` in
  `project.yaml`): an ID from `manifests/image-providers.json`.
- `variants` (int, optional, default 2): candidates per sheet.
- `--live` (flag, optional, default off): call the provider. Without it the
  run is a dry run.

## Invokes Agents

- art-director
- character-designer
- environment-designer

## Required Skills

- visual-style-development
- character-sheet-generation
- location-design

## Process

1. Collect the planned sheets from the bibles and order them. The look page
   comes first, because every other sheet is drawn in that style. Then each
   character's turnaround, then the expression and wardrobe sheets that
   condition on the approved turnaround, then location plates and props. A
   sheet whose parent is not `approved` is blocked. On a "next" from the
   user with a parent still in review, state the blocker and ask for the
   verdict.
2. Check the bible entries each sheet is compiled from. A sheet is drawn for
   reading, in the comic's own drawing style: faces clear, background
   plain, scale consistent between views, dramatic lighting kept for the
   pages. The compiler writes that brief; the entity file supplies the
   subject. A recurring secondary character gets at least a turnaround.
   Characters listed in each other's `visually_adjacent_to` get the
   difference stated in both sheets, taken from their
   `distinguishing_features`.
3. Compile one prompt package per sheet:
   `node scripts/compile-prompts.js --asset <ENTITY_ID> --sheet <kind> --root production [--provider <id>] [--model <id>]`.
   The kinds are `turnaround`, `expressions`, and `wardrobe` for a
   character, `plate` for a location, `prop` for a prop, `look` for a look,
   and `detail` with `--subject "<text>"` for a close study of any entity.
   `--outfit <WARD_ID>` picks the outfit of a wardrobe sheet,
   `--expressions a,b,c` the list of an expression sheet, and
   `--time <state>` the time of day of a plate (one of the location's
   `time_of_day_states`, default the first). The script writes an
   asset-scoped package (`page: null`, `asset` set to the entity ID, id
   `PP_<ENTITY_ID>_<PROVIDER>-<TAG>`) to
   `<entity dir>/refs/prompts/<provider>.<kind>.yaml`, and a look page to
   `references/style/prompts/<provider>.<LOOK_ID>.yaml`. A wardrobe sheet
   adds its outfit (`<provider>.wardrobe.<WARD_ID>.yaml`), a detail study a
   slug of its subject (`<provider>.detail.<slug>.yaml`), and a plate for
   a non-default time that state (`<provider>.plate.<state>.yaml`); the
   package ID and the candidate name carry the same variant. It attaches the
   approved look master as a `style` reference and, for expression and
   wardrobe sheets, the character's approved identity master. It refuses a
   sheet while no look master is approved; the first look page is the one
   request compiled without an image. Nothing is written freehand. Each
   outfit and each detail subject has its own package file, so several
   sheets of one entity can be compiled before any is generated.
4. Cost gate: estimate the batch (sheets x variants x provider rate), show
   it, and wait for an explicit confirmation. Run
   `node scripts/generate-assets.js --asset <ENTITY_ID> --root production`
   for the dry run of every sheet package of the entity, or
   `--package <prompt-package.yaml>` for one, and add `--live --yes` only
   after the user confirms. The hook `require-cost-confirmation.js` blocks
   a live call without `--yes`. Each run of a package produces one
   candidate, so `variants` is the number of runs per sheet.
5. Find each returned image where the script put it: the next free
   `<ENTITY_ID>_<TAG>_V##.png` in the entity's `refs/` directory, or
   `production/references/style/<LOOK_ID>_V##.png` for a look page. TAG is
   `TURN`, `EXPR`, `WARD_<OUTFIT>`, `PLATE` (`PLATE_<STATE>` for a
   non-default time), `SHEET` for a prop, or `DETAIL_<SUBJECT>`. A
   candidate never takes a `_MASTER` name. The record and its
   `GEN_*.request.json` are under `production/generations/<ENTITY_ID>/`.
   When the tool does not report the model, the cost, or the seed, the
   record keeps `unreported` or `null` and lists the field in
   `metadata_unavailable`.
6. Open every returned file. The owning designer compares it with the bible:
   each entry of `distinguishing_features`, the wardrobe layers, the map's
   levels and landmarks, the style bible's statements. Pick one candidate
   per sheet or order a re-roll with corrected wording. After the project's
   `repair_policy.max_cycles` rounds without a usable candidate, fix the
   bible text instead of rolling again.
7. Hand the pick to the user with a review card: what the asset is, the
   features to verify taken from the bible, anything this image cannot show,
   and what approving it allows next. The file under review is the
   candidate, still under its candidate name. Wait for an explicit approval
   of that image.
8. Promote the approved pick with
   `node scripts/approve-asset.js --candidate <path-or-stem> --root production [--note "<text>"]`.
   The script copies the candidate to `<ENTITY_ID>_<TAG>_MASTER_V##` (a look
   page to `<LOOK_ID>_MASTER_V##`) with the candidate's version number and
   registers it in `production/references/manifest.yaml` as `approved`:
   `id`, `entity`, `kind`, `path`, `sha256`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`,
   the candidate and generation record it came from, and a single
   `default_role` (`identity` for a turnaround or an expression sheet,
   `style` for a look page, `spatial_continuity` for a plate,
   `prop_consistency` for a prop, `wardrobe` for a wardrobe sheet). It adds
   the asset ID to the entity file's `references`, and for a look master it
   sets `style.look_refs` and `style.style_block` in `project.yaml`, which
   freezes the style block. When the sheet already has an approved master,
   add `--supersede`: the old entry becomes `superseded` and its file stays.
   Run the script only after the user approved the image; it records the
   decision and does not make it. Then move to the next planned sheet
   without waiting to be asked.
9. Run `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root production`, then the
   self-evaluation gates on the manifest entries and generation records.
   Report sheets approved, sheets waiting for a verdict, and spend against
   the estimate.

## Outputs

- `production/characters/<CHAR_ID>/refs/`, `production/locations/<LOC_ID>/refs/`,
  `production/props/<PROP_ID>/refs/`, and `production/references/style/`:
  candidate and master images, with their prompt packages in the `prompts/`
  directory beside them (`schemas/prompt-package.schema.json`).
- `production/references/manifest.yaml`, the registry with the new entries
  (no schema as a whole).
- `production/generations/<ENTITY_ID>/GEN_<ENTITY_ID>_<attempt##>.yaml`, one
  per attempt, with its `.request.json` beside it; validates against
  `schemas/generation-record.schema.json`.
- `references` updated in the entity files, `style.look_refs` in
  `production/project.yaml`.

## Notes

- Cost warning: this is the first command that can spend money. Dry run is
  the default and a live batch always shows its estimate first. Cut
  `variants` before cutting sheets.
- An approved master is immutable. The hook `protect-approved-assets.js`
  refuses edits to it. A change is a new candidate, approved with
  `approve-asset.js --supersede`, which writes the new manifest entry and
  sets `status: superseded` on the old one. The script lists the pages and
  reference plans that still cite the old master; replan and recompile them.
- A photograph or an outside drawing brought in through `/ingest-references`
  informs a sheet through the description its analysis wrote into the
  bible. It does not replace the sheet: identity masters are drawn in the
  comic's style.
- With `harness-native` or `manual` the script writes a handoff package
  (the `GEN_*.request.json`) and calls no network. The harness image tool
  or a person produces the image and saves it at the target path the
  request names, and steps 5 to 8 apply to that file. With `codex-cli` the
  live run starts the Codex CLI and saves the candidate itself.
- fal's default model ignores reference images. Pin a multi-image model
  with `--model` when compiling, or the look master is not used.
- Related: `/character-bible`, `/location-bible`, `/prop-bible`,
  `/style-bible` (plan the sheets), `/reference-plan` (assigns approved
  masters to pages).
